newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm vs dlr, weak on pound.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm vs dlr, weak on pound.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was firm on the dollar on unmatched inflows from traditional exporters but weakened marginally on the pound following trends in the international forex market, commercial bank dealers said on Monday.
Against the dollar, Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean commercial rate of 54.90 compared to 55.01 on Monday, and 91.60 against the pound from 91.04.
Dealers said the overriding sentiment in the market was for a firmer shilling supported largely by inflows from corporations and agricultural exporters.
"Another positive thing is foreign investors are still in the market," one dealer said.
"But we're receiving a lot of buying interest at levels below 55 to the dollar," another dealer said adding that sustained demand at these levels could limit the shillings' gains.
The money market tightened marginally with overnight rates quoted at between 10-11 percent from 8-11 percent on Monday.
